newsitem.title: GERMANY: Germany's Schroeder warns against hasty EMU launch.
newsitem.headline: Germany's Schroeder warns against hasty EMU launch.

text.p: A leading figure in Germany's opposition Social Democrats (SPD) said on Thursday fulfilling the criteria for European economic and monetary union (EMU) was far more important than the timetable.

Gerhard Schroeder, premier of Lower Saxony and a likely opponent of Chancellor Helmut Kohl in general elections next year, said he strongly disagreed with other German leaders who warn of disastrous consequences if the euro is delayed.

In an interview with ZDF television to be broadcast on Thursday evening, Schroeder said the question of whether the euro would be launched on schedule in 1999 depended on whether enough nations could meet the fiscal criteria set out by the Maastricht Treaty.

"I urge that we emphasise fulfilling the criteria before the timetable," Schroeder said. He rejected claims by many leaders, including Chancellor Helmut Kohl and former Chancellor Helmut Schmidt, that delaying the euro's launch could mean its ruin.

"I just cannot share the catastrophic scenarios as they are being portrayed," he said. "European integration sometimes moves ahead quickly, sometimes slowly." He said the euro would lead to more unemployment in Germany in the short and medium term, but that would change over the longer term.

"Those who believe that the euro will create more jobs in the short and medium term are wrong -- the exact opposite will happen," Schroeder said. "The long-term development will be more favourable." That was why he supported the euro, he said.
